$comment: THE PRODUCT'S NUMBERS, IN ONE PLACE.
Every value here is written by hand in several other files: the copy
catalogue, the worker's message templates, the terms of use, the billing
FAQ and the legal brief. That duplication is not going away — a price in
`termos-de-uso.md` has to be prose, not a placeholder, because it is a
contract clause — so the answer is not to generate those files but to be
able to prove they still agree. `apps/web/lib/product.test.ts` does that:
it fails, naming the file, when any of them drifts from this one.
Why it exists: D11b was three hardcoded dates, D7 was one claim in four
places, D6 survived a guard that keyed on the wrong phrasing. Each was a
product fact typed by hand in more places than anyone could hold in their
head, and each was found by a person reading one screen closely.
Changing a number here does NOT change what renders. It changes the test
from green to red, listing every site still carrying the old value.
Money is in whole BRL. Dates are ISO, in the product's clock
(America/Sao_Paulo) — see CLAUDE.md on the three clocks.
